newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson Dec same-store sales down.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson Dec same-store sales down.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said its comparable-store sales for the five weeks ended January 4, 1997 decreased three percent from the same period a year ago.
Net retail sales increased 3.5 percent to $4.238 billion from $4.096 billion a year ago, it said.
"December sales at Target and Mervyn's met our expectations, while sales at the department store division were slightly below plan," said chief executive Bob Ulrich.
"As a result, overall performance of the corporation remains in line with previous expectations," he said.
December and year-to-date sales by operating division were as follows:

-- Target's total sales for the month increased 8.2 percent and same-store sales decreased 0.3 percent. Year-to-date, Target's total sales increased 14.5 percent and same-store sales increased 5.7 percent.

-- Mervyn's total sales for the month decreased 9.1 percent and same-store sales decreased 10.1 percent. Year-to-date, Mervyn's total sales decreased 2.6 percent and same-store sales decreased 4.3 percent.

-- The department store division's total sales for the month decreased 4.6 percent and same-store sales decreased 7.7 percent. Year-to-date, department stores total sales decreased 1.3 percent and same-store sales decreased 4.9 percent.
Total company sales for the 48 weeks ended January 4, 1997 were $23.40 billion, up 9.1 percent from $21.44 billion in the same period a year ago, the company said.
Same-store sales for the 48-week period were up 2.4 percent compared to the same period last year.
